extraction.name: FLEURS: Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech
extraction.description: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.publisher: Meta AI Research, Google Research, Carnegie Mellon University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection starts with the FLoRes-101 dataset. For each sentence in the 102 languages, three recordings were collected by three different native speakers. Each recording was then evaluated by additional workers to assess whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In the first version of the dataset, about 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw text data comes from the FLoRes-101 dataset, which contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by human translators. The raw speech data consists of recordings by native speakers.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All recordings are kept as they-are, either from quiet or noisy environment, without any data augmentations (e.g., SpecAugment, speed perturbation, simulated reverberation, etc.).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For textual data, NFC and then FST normalization is applied to each sentence, lower-cased, normalized and punctuations removed. Words are split into characters, and the token | is defined as word boundaries.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each recording is evaluated by additional workers to assess whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings are discarded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Invalid recordings are discarded, leaving between zero and three recordings per sentence in the final dataset.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Native speakers, imposing a balance in terms of sex ratio of at least 30/70%, when possible.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to fill the missing data gaps in future versions of the dataset.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Sex (gender) and native language/geography of the speakers.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The goal of FLEURS is to enable speech technology in more languages and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding, enabling progress towards building speech technologies for everyone.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: About 21.5% of the sentences are missing in the first version. Recordings include noisy environments. Tokenization mismatches and unrepresented scripts (e.g., Odia) can affect model performance.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation, and Retrieval (Speech-to-Text, Text-to-Speech, Speech-to-Speech).
